title: Overdue Interest Carried in a Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Catch-Up Payment
content:
**Collections desk calculation, Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract — interest carried for days beyond the grace period.**

**Rule.** The per diem is the contract's principal balance times its APR divided by 100 and by the product's day basis of 365 days, rounded to the cent, and the days beyond grace are the calendar days from the contract's next due date to today less the product's grace period of 10 days. When the days beyond grace are at least 5, the catch-up amount also carries the per diem for every day beyond grace; when they are from 1 to fewer than 5, it carries the per diem for one day; in every other case it carries no interest. The interest carried is the per diem times those days, rounded to the cent.

The day basis (365) and the grace period (10 days) are the same on Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Tier 5, Tier 4, Tier 3, Tier 2, Tier 1 and Tier 1+. The interest carried is added to the catch-up amount.

**Counting.** A count of calendar days from one date to another is the second date less the first, so the first date is not counted and the second is; the count is zero or negative when the second date is not after the first.

| Days from the next due date to today | Days beyond grace | Days of interest carried |
|---|---|---|
| 15 or more | 5 or more | every day beyond grace |
| 11 to 14 | 1 to 4 | one day |
| 10 or fewer | 0 or fewer | none |

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Principal balance 14,600.00 dollars at an APR of 7.50 percent: the per diem is 14,600.00 times 7.50 divided by 100 and by 365, which is 3.00 dollars.

- 22 days after the due date (12 beyond grace): 12 days, 36.00 dollars carried.
- 13 days after the due date (3 beyond grace): one day, 3.00 dollars.
- 9 days after the due date: nothing carried.
